subject: mathematics
question_text: The points A, B and C have position vectors −2i + j − k, −4i + 2j + 2k and 6i − 3j − 13k respectively, and AB = λ AC. Find the value of λ.

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), book p.61, chapter 6 ADDITION OF VECTORS, Very Short Answer question 10. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The 1+1 shape is the one this bank uses for a Maths-1A Section A question: the first mark is for building AB and AC from the three position vectors, the second for comparing components and solving for λ. This book prints almost no exam-appearance years, so appearances[] is empty — Addition of Vectors has long been examined, we simply have no sourced years for this question. Paper position: Maths-1A Section A runs Q1 to Q10 at 2 marks each, all compulsory, under the 2026-27 pattern. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. The value λ = −1/4 was checked against all three components before it was written: −2 = 8λ, 1 = −4λ and 3 = −12λ each give −1/4.

recall_prompt: Say how you would find λ when one vector is a multiple of another.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Find AB and AC
steps.margin_note: First mark. AB is head minus tail: the position vector of B minus the position vector of A. Watch the double minus — subtracting −2i adds 2i.
steps.memory_tip: AB = OB − OA, always head minus tail. Subtracting −2i adds 2i, and subtracting −k adds k.

recall.must_convey: That AB = OB − OA = −2i + j + 3k and AC = OC − OA = 8i − 4j − 12k.
accept: subtract the position vector of A from each of B and C
AB is minus two i plus j plus three k and AC is eight i minus four j minus twelve k
head minus tail so B minus A and C minus A
OB minus OA cheste AB vasthundi, alaage AC
build the two vectors from the position vectors first
heard_as: minus two i plus j plus three k

steps.why: The condition given is about the vectors joining the points, not about the position vectors themselves, so both AB and AC have to be built from a common starting point A.
common_mistakes: Writing AB as OA − OB, which reverses every sign.
Losing a double minus and getting −6i in AB.
Comparing OB with OC instead of AB with AC.

steps.label: Compare components and solve
steps.margin_note: Second mark. One component fixes λ, but write the other two as well: all three must give the same number, and that is what makes A, B and C lie on one line.
steps.memory_tip: Solve λ from one component, then confirm with the other two. All three must give the same value, here −1/4.

recall.must_convey: That comparing the i, j and k components each gives λ = −1/4.
accept: compare the components, minus two equals eight lambda so lambda is minus one by four
all three components give lambda equals minus a quarter
equate coefficients of i j and k and solve
components compare cheste lambda minus one by four vasthundi
lambda is minus one fourth and the other two components agree

steps.why: λ is a single number, so the i, the j and the k comparison must all return the same value. Checking all three is the proof that AB really is a multiple of AC.
common_mistakes: Writing λ = −4 by turning the fraction upside down.
Dropping the minus sign and answering 1/4.
Using one component only and never checking the other two.
